sources.title: Public inspection and precedential status of written determinations
sources.legal_status: Statutory rule, subject to its exceptions
sources.summary: Written determinations include rulings, determination letters, technical advice memoranda, and Chief Counsel advice. The general rule bars their use as precedent.
sources.limitations: Do not confuse precedential status with separate regulatory penalty standards. The statute contains an express regulatory exception and a subtitle D qualification.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed

sources.title: Finality and nonprecedential status of small tax cases
sources.legal_status: Statutory limit on review and precedent
sources.summary: A decision in a proceeding conducted under this section is not reviewable in another court and is not precedent for another case.
sources.limitations: Confirm that the proceeding actually used small tax case procedures; a small dollar amount alone is insufficient.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed

sources.title: Rules and regulations
sources.summary: The statute authorizes tax regulations, supplies applicability-date rules and exceptions, and provides a three-year expiration limit for temporary regulations.
sources.limitations: Section-specific delegations and effective-date provisions may matter; a date comparison alone cannot resolve retroactivity.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed

sources.title: Review of Tax Court decisions
sources.summary: Court-of-appeals review and venue depend on statutory conditions; residence or business location is not the only possible venue rule.
sources.limitations: This source identifies review routes; it is not a complete procedural deadline guide or a determination of controlling precedent in a particular case.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed

sources.title: Scope of judicial review of agency action
sources.summary: Courts decide legal questions presented on review and examine agency action against statutory and procedural limits.
sources.limitations: The provision does not supply a universal jurisdictional basis or replace tax-specific review procedures.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed

sources.title: Substantial authority and evaluation of tax authorities
sources.legal_status: Regulatory penalty standard, separate from precedent
sources.summary: Authority evaluation is contextual, considers opposing sources, and includes qualifying PLRs and TAMs. Geographic applicability has a special rule.
sources.limitations: Editorial weights cannot establish substantial authority. CCA is not expressly enumerated. The regulation must be read with current statutes and all applicable exceptions.
sources.currency_observed: Title 26 displayed current through 2026-11-19; eCFR is authoritative but unofficial

sources.title: Tax code, regulations and official guidance
sources.pinpoint: Discussion of Internal Revenue Bulletin precedents
sources.summary: Published rulings and procedures differ from regulations; subsequent developments and factual similarity affect their use.
sources.limitations: This navigation page explains sources but is not itself the underlying controlling statute, regulation, or court holding.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Understanding forms of tax guidance
sources.pinpoint: Regulation; Revenue ruling; Revenue procedure; Private letter ruling; Technical advice memorandum
sources.summary: Rulings generally address substantive applications, procedures address administrative methods, and a taxpayer-specific ruling depends on the actual facts and conditions.
sources.limitations: The overview is a starting point; verify current annual ruling procedures for any actual ruling request.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Tax Court opinion categories and post-trial guidance
sources.pinpoint: Question: Does the Tax Court issue different types of opinions?
sources.legal_status: Court explanation of its opinion categories
sources.summary: Regular and memorandum opinions may be cited as legal authority; summary and bench opinions cannot be relied on as precedent.
sources.limitations: Citable does not mean controlling for every forum, issue, or taxpayer. Subsequent history still requires review.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Internal Revenue Manual process
sources.summary: The manual is the official compilation of staff instructions; interim guidance can change operational instructions.
sources.limitations: Internal procedural status must not be represented as legislation or a regulation binding every tribunal.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Researching tax law and evaluating source categories
sources.summary: Outdated regulations require care; publications supply general information rather than binding positions; judicial history and guidance categories require separate review.
sources.limitations: Some subsections carry older revision dates. Follow the primary law where an internal explanation differs.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Supreme Court statutory-interpretation decision, docket 22-451
sources.pinpoint: Decision dated 2024-06-28, opinion pp. 34-35; official PDF pp. 42-43
sources.legal_status: Supreme Court decision on statutory interpretation
sources.summary: Courts exercise independent judgment on statutory meaning; ambiguity alone does not require acceptance of an agency interpretation. Lawful delegations remain relevant.
sources.limitations: Neutral docket metadata is used to honor the naming restriction. This is not a case-specific opinion on the validity of any tax regulation.

sources.title: Court-of-appeals discussion of manual status, docket 20-72416
sources.legal_status: Circuit judicial treatment of internal manual guidance
sources.summary: The opinion distinguishes internal procedural instructions from law creating taxpayer rights.
sources.limitations: A circuit opinion must be evaluated in its jurisdiction and factual context; the package does not claim an exhaustive subsequent-history search.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Reliance on published guidance and frequently asked questions
sources.pinpoint: Frequently asked questions and reasonable reliance
sources.legal_status: Agency explanation of information and penalty reliance
sources.summary: Reasonable good-faith FAQ reliance can matter under applicable penalty standards. FAQs in a Fact Sheet linked to an agency news release are considered authority for substantial-authority analysis.
sources.limitations: Ordinary informational material and qualifying published fact-sheet FAQs require different classifications. Neither becomes binding law merely from website publication.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Overview of the tax regulations process
sources.summary: Proposed, temporary, and final regulations represent distinct procedural stages and require separate status labels.
sources.limitations: A proposal is not automatically an effective final rule; any authorized reliance and applicability dates require a source-specific check.
sources.currency_observed: Not represented as a complete subsequent-history check

sources.title: Introduction and penalty relief
sources.legal_status: Internal administrative instructions, not a statute
sources.summary: FTA scope and prior-account checks, qualifying reversals, exclusions, correct errors first, and continuing failure-to-pay accrual.
sources.limitations: Read with the 2026 AEP procedural update; redacted internal thresholds are not implemented.

sources.title: Automatic Exemption From Penalty Administrative Relief
sources.summary: Defines original-return timing, current eligible forms, compliance indicators, manual correction and the transition from FTA.
sources.limitations: No source pages or internal marked text are redistributed; manual eligibility remains an IRS determination.

sources.title: Automatic Exemption from Penalty: What taxpayers should know
sources.pinpoint: FS-2026-12, July 2026; First Time Abate transition
sources.summary: AEP begins during 2026; FTA ends for original returns due on or after 2027-01-01.
sources.limitations: Summary guidance cannot replace period-specific procedural criteria.

sources.title: Administrative penalty relief
sources.pinpoint: FTA, AEP, eligible penalties, qualification, and comparison sections
sources.summary: Lists narrow eligible penalty provisions and describes automatic nonassessment and continued liability for tax and interest.
sources.limitations: The procedural update supplies details omitted from the public summary.

sources.title: Consequences of not filing
sources.summary: Legacy FTA checks current return filing or valid extensions and payment or payment arrangements; full payment is not always required before requesting FTA.
sources.limitations: This page predates the AEP transition; its legacy FTA conditions are not imposed on AEP.

sources.title: Penalty relief for reasonable cause
sources.pinpoint: Reasonable cause; failure to file or pay; accuracy-related penalties
sources.summary: Circumstances and the applicable statute matter; illness or disaster is evidence to evaluate, while a reason label or lack of money alone does not establish relief.
sources.limitations: General summaries omit penalty-specific exceptions and procedural details.

sources.title: Failure to file tax return or to pay tax
sources.legal_status: Treasury regulation, subject to statute and controlling judicial interpretation
sources.summary: Ordinary care, inability to comply, financial circumstances and undue hardship inform the late-filing and late-payment exception.
sources.limitations: The model does not compute extension-period presumptions or penalty amounts.

sources.title: Failure to file tax return or to pay tax
sources.summary: These three provisions distinguish late filing, unpaid reported tax, and unpaid tax not originally shown; each has a reasonable-cause and no-willful-neglect exception.
sources.limitations: Rates, inflation adjustments, collection notices and computation are outside the model.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Failure to make deposit of taxes
sources.summary: Deposit failures have a statutory reasonable-cause and no-willful-neglect exception.
sources.limitations: Deposit schedules, computation, allocations, and other statutory deposit exceptions need separate work.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Failure to file partnership return
sources.summary: Late and incomplete partnership returns are distinct; reasonable cause is a statutory exception.
sources.limitations: FTA includes the late-return provision, not every failure described in this section.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Failure to file S corporation return
sources.summary: Late and incomplete S corporation returns are distinct; reasonable cause is a statutory exception.
sources.limitations: FTA includes the late-return provision, not every failure described in this section.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Definitions and special rules
sources.summary: Reasonable cause plus good faith can protect covered underpayments, with express component-specific exclusions and special valuation rules.
sources.limitations: Economic-substance and section 6662(b)(10) exclusions apply; reportable transactions need a separate analysis.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Reasonable cause and good faith exception to section 6662 penalties
sources.legal_status: Treasury regulation, subject to later statutory limits
sources.summary: The taxpayer effort, relevant circumstances and reasonableness of informed professional reliance matter.
sources.limitations: Advice reliance is not automatic protection and must be tested against current statute.

sources.title: Failure by individual to pay estimated income tax
sources.summary: Special waiver grounds include unusual circumstances where assessment would be inequitable and certain recent retirement or disability cases with reasonable cause.
sources.limitations: Other exceptions, safe harbors, and payment computations are not determined by the two-waiver screen.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Estimated tax penalties
sources.summary: Separates ordinary reasonable cause from the narrow statutory waiver and describes a supported request and review.
sources.limitations: Read the statute first; not every hardship is a statutory waiver.

sources.title: Waiver; definitions and special rules
sources.summary: Covered information-reporting penalties can be waived for reasonable cause and no willful neglect.
sources.limitations: International reporting provisions may have different statutes and are not covered simply by this section.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Reasonable cause
sources.summary: Significant mitigating factors or events beyond control must be accompanied by responsible conduct before and after the failure.
sources.limitations: The executable model refers these cases for penalty-specific review rather than applying late-payment rules.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 843
sources.pinpoint: Revision 12/2024; Purpose of Form, Where To File, Separate Form Required
sources.summary: Form 843 can address certain penalty claims; the proper form, separate-period treatment and submission location depend on the request.
sources.limitations: Not a substitute for an amended return or every tax refund claim; check notice and current instructions.

sources.title: Abatements
sources.summary: Interest abatement and erroneous written-advice relief have specific statutory conditions distinct from ordinary penalty relief.
sources.limitations: The executable model does not decide these separate claims.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Limitations on credit or refund
sources.summary: Separates the time for filing a credit or refund claim from the amount recoverable under the applicable payment lookback. A timely claim does not alone establish that every payment is within the recoverable period.
sources.limitations: General statutory framework only. Special extensions, suspension provisions, deemed payment dates, claim type, and procedural facts require separate analysis.
sources.currency_observed: Laws in effect through 2026-11-10, as displayed on the current section page

sources.title: Extensions of time to file an individual return
sources.pinpoint: Topic 304, ordinary automatic extension; distinguish special payment extensions
sources.summary: An ordinary extension of time to file does not extend the time to pay the tax. Filing and payment obligations should be analyzed separately.
sources.limitations: Special statutory or administrative payment extensions and overseas rules require separate review. The question concerns only an ordinary filing extension.

sources.title: Penalty relief and response procedures
sources.pinpoint: Notice accuracy; How to request penalty relief; How to appeal; Interest relief
sources.summary: Directs taxpayers to verify notice information, follow notice instructions, and identify the penalty and grounds for relief. Describes telephone requests, possible written requests, and corresponding adjustments to interest on reduced penalties.
sources.limitations: Does not supply one universal deadline or form for every penalty. Read the actual notice and current applicable instructions before acting.
